}\n\nstatic ThreadGrid chooseThreadGrid(const size_t interiorZ, const size_t interiorY, const size_t nth) {\n    ThreadGrid best{std::max<size_t>(1, std::min(interiorZ, nth)), 1};\n    size_t bestCost = ceilDiv(interiorZ, best.pz) * ceilDiv(interiorY, best.py);\n    for (size_t py = 1; a flat parallel sweep keeps the identical values while\n    // matching the first-touch page distribution.\n    #pragma omp parallel for schedule(static)\n    for (size_t idx = 0; idx < total; ++idx) {\n        g[idx] = static_cast<Real>(idx % 19) * 1.0;\n    }\n}\n\n// One interior row of the 7-point stencil. The split is chosen to minimize the busiest thread's work, so it's even to within one plane/row — no schedule-induced imbalance. Slab ownership is contiguous in memory, so it matches the pages each thread first-touched.\n\n**Cache blocking** — within its region a thread walks z inside a y-block sized so the three live planes (~256 KiB) stay in a core's private cache, turning the z-neighbour loads into hits.\n\n**Boundary copy** — the original rescanned the whole grid with a boundary predicate (O(N) for O(N^2/3) work). Now only the two z-faces plus each interior plane's frame are copied; identical result, ~1% of the cost.\n\n**NUMA first touch** — grids are `reserve`d and touched in parallel with the same static distribution before `resize`, so pages land on the right node (the default `std::vector` constructor would put everything on node 0). `initializeGrid` is a flat parallel sweep — the initial value depends only on the linear index, so values are unchanged.\n\n**Thread pinning** — libgomp reads `OMP_PROC_BIND` before `main`, so the program pins threads itself via `sched_getaffinity` + `/sys` sibling topology + `pthread_setaffinity_np`: one thread per physical core, spread across NUMA nodes, respecting cpusets and any explicit user affinity/thread-count request. Worth ~2.5x here.\n\n**Non-temporal stores** — AVX2 `_mm256_stream_pd` for the aligned bulk of each row when the grids exceed the aggregate L3, removing read-for-ownership traffic (+30% at 512³); regular stores below that threshold, where keeping output cached wins (2x at 256³). Summation order and the `/ 7.0` division are preserved exactly, so results are bit-identical.\n\n**One parallel region for the whole run** — per-iteration sync is a single barrier instead of a fork/join (2-3x on small grids).\n\nValidation and the min/max/NaN scans are parallelized too. CMake now does `find_package(OpenMP REQUIRED)` and links `OpenMP::OpenMP_CXX`; executable name unchanged.\n\n## Results (dual EPYC 7763, 128 cores)\n\n| Grid | Serial | OpenMP | Speedup |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 128³ ×100 | 446 ms | 9 ms | 50× |\n| 256³ ×30 | 1106 ms | 16 ms | 69× |\n| 512³ ×10 | 3145 ms | 89 ms | 35× |\n\n512³ sustains ~240 GB/s, ~80% of the machine's measured stream bandwidth.
